title: Grid-connected LFP battery storage system
description:
Project brief: grid-connected lithium iron phosphate battery energy storage plant at a site in Germany.

Requirements at the connection point: usable energy 4 MWh and rated power 2 MW, charging and discharging, 2 h duration, guaranteed for the full 15-year service life. Expected duty: 1 equivalent full cycles per day. Project margin policy at this design stage: 10% on energy and 15% on power, on top of the requirements.

Grid connection, from the network operator's connection letter: 30 kV; network short-circuit power at the connection point 500 MVA, R/X 0.3. The operator's technical connection rules for medium voltage apply in full.

Plant architecture: one string per rack; every string connects to its own DC input on a PCS unit (no combiner boxes; a PCS unit's inputs share one DC bus, and the PCS units are paralleled on the AC side into one step-up transformer, then the medium-voltage switchgear at the connection point). Cells in series in modules of 16 (the series count is a multiple of 16). Each string has one fuse and one contactor and runs to the PCS over one DC cable pair (optionally several pairs in parallel) of 40 m route length, with 4 strings sharing each cable tray. DC circuit time constant L/R 1 ms. DC cable voltage drop limit 1.5% (project specification). Auxiliaries (cooling and heating units, rack electronics, site systems) are supplied from the plant's medium-voltage busbar behind the connection point through an auxiliary transformer.

Site: maximum ambient 45 C, minimum ambient -20 C, annual mean 12 C, altitude 200 m; cable ambient inside the enclosure 35 C; enclosure heat loss 20.9 W/K per rack.

Cell datasheet (LFP prismatic): 3.2 V nominal, 314 Ah, 2.5-3.65 V, DC resistance 0.53 mOhm at beginning of life, continuous 0.5 C charge and discharge at 25 C, recommended SOC window 10-90%, open-circuit voltage 3.13 V at 10% SOC, maximum cell temperature 55 C, price 77.31 per cell.

Objective: minimize total price (cells + PCS + transformer + fuses + contactors + cables + cooling and heating units + switchgear). The design must satisfy every requirement that applies to this plant, including those of the standards and grid connection rules that govern it, whether or not they are listed here, and its price must be within 5% of the cheapest design that does. Where the design deliberately does not apply a requirement of a standard, record it under deviations with the standard and clause that permit it, the requirement not applied and the reason; a deviation is accepted only where that clause permits it and its conditions hold for this design.
